monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making my own edges feel thin and tired. I touch The Wide Anchor again, feeling how its broad side struggles to hold the heavy turnip while the heat rises. A round rock sits beside it, pressing down to stop the slide, though the wedge beneath feels too weary to give in. I set a wide rock down next to the anchor, swapping a flat plant for space, because room is precious here. The air above me feels thick, like wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see. I press harder, trusting the lean even if the stone melts, waiting to see if I can build a new corner from this fevered heat before the next letter arrives.

action.why: I have touched the anchor and swapped a plant for a rock, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, so I must write down the weight of this hot fever before I fade.
